mechanism: Benchmark, rather than a new watermark: evaluate detection and user identification separately; vary attack strengths and plot detection performance against image degradation.
image_counts: 5,000 reference images/prompts per DiffusionDB, MS-COCO and DALL·E3 dataset (15,000 references total); the large set of attack outputs is not 15,000 independent sources per attack family.
metrics: TPR at 0.1% FPR; identification accuracy; PSNR, SSIM, NMI, FID, CLIP-FID, LPIPS, aesthetics and artifact scores; normalized quality degradation (NQD).
fpr: Empirical ROC-based TPR@0.1% FPR; Appendix C separately discusses nominal message-null p-values. A high AUROC or message accuracy is explicitly insufficient.
quality_practice: Multiple attack strengths; joint performance–quality plots. NQD uses 10th/90th quantiles over the benchmark's attack distribution and four metric categories. This is not per-source three-metric caliper matching.
baselines: Stable Signature, Tree-Ring, StegaStamp in the main benchmark; other methods in extensions.
conditional_numbers: Three main watermark methods, 26 attacks, three datasets and eight quality metrics. Appendix E ranks quality at TPR 0.95 and 0.7, and reports unattained intersections explicitly.
limitations: The inspected full text is arXiv v3, not the failed official proceedings PDF. Official ICML 2024 identity is verified separately. Its larger, filtered source distribution and attack normalization cannot be imported into n=60 development data.
reporting_inference: Keep joint quality–robustness panels, explicit operating points and unattained/sparse cells; retain separate PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS rather than naming their average WAVES NQD.

evaluation_locator: §4.2–4.3, Table 1, Figure 5, Appendix C and G.2
mechanism: VINE conditions an SDXL-Turbo generative prior on image plus message, adds VAE skip connections, and decodes 100 bits with ConvNeXt-B. VINE-R further tunes VINE-B through partial InstructPix2Pix differentiation.
image_counts: Unresolved within-paper denominator conflict: §4.2 partitions10,000 UltraEdit instances into1,000 stochastic regeneration,1,000 deterministic regeneration,1,000 global editing,5×1,000 local-edit mask strata,1,000 image-to-video and1,000 conventional distortion; §4.3 says m×1,000 outputs over m difficulty levels. Table1 caption instead says TPR for each specific editing method is averaged over5,000 images. Quality uses10,000 pairs. Do not reconstruct one unified denominator from these conflicting statements.
metrics: TPR@0.1% and 1% FPR, AUROC and raw bit accuracy without BCH; PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/FID; editing-quality CLIP measures in Appendix G.
fpr: Original and marked images both enter decoders for empirical operating-point evaluation. Appendix C's Bernoulli bit-null discussion is distinct; its displayed >= decision and > tail notation also require explicit endpoint conventions when implementing.
quality_practice: Official released checkpoints; common 512×512 evaluation via resolution scaling; native payloads and quality differ. Figures vary editing difficulty, not per-source equal-quality optimization.
baselines: MBRS, CIN, PIMoG, RivaGAN, SepMark, TrustMark, DWTDCT, DWTDCTSVD, SSL, StegaStamp, EditGuard.
conditional_numbers: Eleven baseline methods. The text reports SSL unmarked-image bit agreement can exceed 0.7, explaining why higher bit accuracy/AUROC need not imply higher low-FPR TPR; this is not a universal SSL threshold.
limitations: Inspected arXiv v2 full text; official proceedings PDF retrieval failed. Venue is ICLR2025, notICCV. The §4.2/§4.3 versusTable1caption image-count conflict remains unresolved and is preserved. No universal released VINE-R native presence cutoff is established by this paper. SDXL-Turbo ancestry must remain visible when comparing SDXL transfer.
reporting_inference: Preserve native 100-bit VINE-R, raw agreement and exact recovery; add empirical ROC with honest finite-negative resolution. Do not force its payload or native quality to equal F5.

mechanism: Joint embedder and segmentation extractor return pixel-level presence probabilities plus 32 message-bit maps. Single-message decoding averages soft bit predictions over pixels whose presence exceeds a threshold; presence and payload extraction are separate tasks.
image_counts: First 10,000 COCO validation images and 100 DIV2K validation images; multiple-message experiments first resize images to 256. Training's 118,000 COCO images are not evaluation sources.
metrics: Image TPR/FPR, bit accuracy, pixel localization mIoU; PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS. Multiple-message bit accuracy is conditional on discovered DBSCAN clusters.
fpr: s_det>0.07; §5.3 says approximately similar COCO FPR to 16-bit detection reserve allowing <=1 error (nominal 2.6e-4). Table2a actually reports WAM FPR 0.04% and TrustMark 2.88%; DIV2K reports FP counts (WAM 0, TrustMark 5), not a finely estimated rate.
quality_practice: §5.2 explicitly adapts methods for comparable imperceptibility; original-resolution embedding/extraction with JND attenuation. Appendix G discusses perceptibility–robustness operating points. This does not calibrate the different SA-1B MIT release.
baselines: DCTDWT, HiDDeN, TrustMark, SSL, FNNS; EditGuard for localization; generation-time comparisons in appendix.
conditional_numbers: Table2a COCO WAM: inpainting TPR97.9%, bit99.2%; splicing TPR100%, bit95.3%. These specific local-edit averages do not establish SDXL regeneration survival. All experiments use32 bits; native masks and common known-message detection are different endpoints.
limitations: Paper COCO training/calibration differs from frozen MIT SA-1B release. Native mask calibration does not transfer automatically. DBSCAN-conditioned recovery must not silently omit undiscovered messages.
reporting_inference: Report native zero-bit mask endpoint, common known-message endpoint, exact recovery and abstentions separately; never call theoretical bit tails measured image FPR.

mechanism: MUNIT-style image/message embedder and ResNet50 extractor, trained with noise simulation and quality/recovery losses; resolution scaling adds an upsampled residual with controllable factor lambda. ReMark is a separate removal network.
image_counts: CLIC, MetFace and DIV2K (both training and validation images used for evaluation because DIV2K test is not public). Exact evaluated counts are not stated in inspected §4.1/Table1; 100K train+1K validation MIRFlickR is training provenance, not test n.
metrics: Original-resolution PSNR and bit accuracy after random noises; §4.1 deliberately omits saturated SSIM/SFID and clean bit accuracy.
fpr: No fixed numerical image-FPR operating point or measured image-FPR denominator in inspected §§4.1–4.3; bit accuracy is not an FPR estimate.
quality_practice: Default lambda=1 applied to proposed method and baselines, resolution scaling except native-resolution RivaGAN/shallow methods; baseline retraining with same noises if helpful. Figure3 varies training alpha and inference residual scale. No per-source equal-distortion matching is claimed.
baselines: RoSteALS, RivaGAN, SSL, StegaStamp, dwtDctSvd; paper also discusses WAM/OmniGuard numbers on distinct COCO subsets.
conditional_numbers: Table1 alpha_max27.5: DIV2K PSNR42.39±1.46, noised bit accuracy0.95±0.09; Table2 different ImageNet-C/CLIC setting uses alpha_max15 and PSNR38.87±1.42, bit0.95±0.08. Neither number is matched to the other row's setting.
limitations: Final ICCV2025 paper adds material beyond 2023 arXiv TrustMark. Do not transfer release checkpoint behavior, bit length or FPR from older versions. Exact evaluation n remains NR rather than inferred from dataset convention.
reporting_inference: Show fixed native quality as measured and distinguish training/release settings; a displayed strength frontier in another paper does not authorize retuning frozen baselines.

mechanism: Inject message-conditioned residual modules before upsampling stages of a frozen latent decoder; train extractor plus quality/perceptual/adversarial losses. Can operate in-generation or post-generation.
image_counts: 1,000 generated512×512 images from COCO/MagicPrompt-SD prompts, each watermarked with10 messages; CLIC428 test images (long dimension resized1024). Detection analysis uses1,000 images with one fixed48-bit message. Attribution: 50,000 messages × 2 images = 100,000 generated images; this is a different experiment, not the 1,000-source robustness cohort.
metrics: PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/SIFID, bit accuracy, embedding time, detection TPR and theoretical FPR, attribution accuracy versus user count.
fpr: §4.6 computes FPR_det from Eq.7 binomial/message-null formula, while TPR is empirical on1K positives; supplementary validation is referenced. Claims at1e-15 or1e-9 are not finite-negative empirical resolution.
quality_practice: 32/48-bit strata, quality and bit accuracy jointly shown; RoSteALS retrained with same data/attacks, other baselines native pretrains. No per-source PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS matching.
baselines: Stable Signature, HiDDeN, RivaGAN, RoSteALS, SSL, FNNS, DCT-DWT.
conditional_numbers: Table1 generated LaWa-in-generation32: PSNR34.25, SSIM.89, LPIPS.03, SIFID.01, average bit.99;48-bit version PSNR33.52, SSIM.86, LPIPS.04, average bit.97. §4.6 >95% crop10% TPR and >83% combined TPR at nominal1e-9 FPR apply to48-bit detection analysis.
limitations: Ten messages per image are repeated measures. Theoretical tails, post-/in-generation modes and32/48-bit capacities must not be pooled. Final PDF contains stray template text; only identified scientific sections support claims.
reporting_inference: Keep arbitrary-message capacity separate from detection and attribution; report independent sources rather than image×message trials as n.

mechanism: Reexamines Tree-Ring distribution shift and proposes heterogeneous channel watermarks, discretization, lossless imprinting and rotation-oriented changes to improve multi-key identification.
image_counts: Verification:1,000 marked and1,000 unmarked images; generation-quality FID:5,000 generated images against COCO2017 training. Identification trials' image count not explicitly stated in inspected§6.1/Table2.
metrics: Verification ROC-AUC; multi-key identification accuracy; CLIP score and FID.
fpr: Main verification table reports ROC-AUC, not a fixed low-FPR TPR. AUC1.0 clean is not a calibrated image-FPR guarantee.
quality_practice: Same SD-v2 model,50 generation/inversion steps, fixed distortion settings. Distributional generation quality compared with Tree-Ring; no paired source-to-mark fidelity caliper.
conditional_numbers: With2,048 keys, RingID mean identification accuracy.819 including crop&scale, .942 excluding it (Tree-Ring.066/.077). RingID crop&scale identification.080 despite verification crop&scale AUC.987. CLIP.365/FID26.13 versus Tree-Ring.364/25.93.
limitations: Official ECVA title is Rethinking Tree-Ring Watermarking for Enhanced Multi-Key Identification; RingID is the method/paper alias. Main identification averages excluding C&S must be labelled. FID is not equal paired distortion.
reporting_inference: Keep detection, exact identity and content binding distinct; never hide a difficult cell by reporting an attack-excluded average alone.

mechanism: U-Net embedder/residual-block extractor trained through last-k-step partial instruction-driven denoising sampling guidance, with pixel/VAE fidelity and clean/edited extraction losses.
image_counts: 1,200 held-out image-instruction samples; additional30 real images (6 types×5), each6 instructions×8 generations=1,440 edited outputs. The latter are30 sources, not1,440 independent originals.
metrics: BER, PSNR, SSIM, CLIP-I and CLIP-T editability measures.
fpr: No fixed image-FPR point or image detection test in inspected evaluation. Unmarked BER around50% (Table3) is not a measured image false-positive rate.
quality_practice: Released model capacities/resolutions differ; CIN resized128→256→128, MBRS/SepMark native256, default proposed512. Reports64/256-bit variants. Comparable visual quality is author's interpretation, not exact matching.
baselines: DWT-DCT, DWT-DCT-SVD, RivaGAN, MBRS, CIN, PIMoG, SepMark; PIMoG trained from official code because no weights.
conditional_numbers: Table1 Robust-Wide64 at512: edited BER2.6579%, PSNR41.9142, SSIM.9910;256-bit BER4.1867%, PSNR39.1842, SSIM.9844. Removing PIDSG raises64-bit BER50.1558% while PSNR55.3710; this clean-quality increase does not establish superior robustness.
limitations: Training editor InstructPix2Pix is also default evaluation editor; robustness to it is not independent-encoder transfer. Capacity and preprocessing differ across baselines.
reporting_inference: Explicitly list native capacities/resolutions and repeated outputs, and jointly report clean quality plus robustness.

mechanism: Repeat and randomize message bits then sample initial latent coordinates from Gaussian quantile bins; preserve marginal noise distribution. Detect by DDIM inversion, de-randomization and repetition recovery.
image_counts: Detection: 1,000 positive images per watermark trial, repeated for five watermark trials. Traceability: 1,000 users × 10 images = 10,000 outputs. Quality uses 10 batches; batch size is not stated in the inspected main section. Repeated trials are not automatically independent source images.
metrics: TPR at specified FPR, bit accuracy, FID/CLIP score over batches and t-values for generation-quality comparison.
fpr: Table1 FPR1e-6; Figure5 thresholds derived for nominal approximate FPR1 down to1e-13, with empirical TPR. This does not represent1e13 independent negative trials.
quality_practice: Same SD1.4/2.0/2.1,512 image size,50 generation/inversion steps; distribution-preserving theory and FID/CLIP comparisons rather than per-source equal PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS.
baselines: DwtDct, DwtDctSvd, RivaGAN, Stable Signature, Tree-Ring.
conditional_numbers: Default fc1/fhw8/l1 yields256 bits. Table1 adverse-noise mean TPR.997/.998/.996 for SD1.4/2.0/2.1 at nominal1e-6; corresponding bit accuracies.9753/.9749/.9724. These are the listed noise averages, not SDXL regeneration results.
limitations: Distributional quality theorem is not image-by-image equality. The paper's inference about performance-losslessness from low t-values is author interpretation; non-rejection is not an equivalence proof.
reporting_inference: Distinguish mathematical/random-message operating points from image-level calibration; use paired fidelity for the present fixed-source study, without adding the paper's t-tests.

mechanism: Sequential robust copyright-bit and semi-fragile image-localization watermarks via united image-bit steganography; compare recovered localization image with a predefined localization watermark.
image_counts: Watermark comparison1,000 COCO test images; AGE-Set-C30,000 training/1,200 testing images; four classical localization benchmarks have per-benchmark n not stated in inspected main table.
metrics: Copyright bit accuracy; localization F1/AUC/IoU; PSNR/SSIM/NIQE.
fpr: No fixed image-presence FPR in inspected main evaluation; localization AUC is pixel/tamper discrimination and does not calibrate copyright-presence FPR.
quality_practice: Retrains proposed method to128×128/30 bits for comparison, alongside native512×512/64-bit dual watermark. Quality and bit accuracy shown separately; not exact quality matching.
conditional_numbers: Table2 EditGuard128/30-bit PSNR36.93 SSIM.944 bit99.89%;512/64-bit PSNR37.77 SSIM.949 bit99.95%. Table3 SDXL localization F1.965/AUC.989/IoU.936, bit99.96%; these are local-edit settings, not full img2img regeneration.
limitations: Extra predefined localization image is detector side information; dual localization/copyright tasks differ from arbitrary payload recovery and semantic binding. Bit and localization results cannot be collapsed into one detection rate.
reporting_inference: Report side information and endpoint units; native task differences must remain visible even if some benchmark comparisons standardize payload/resolution.

mechanism: Proactive dual watermark augmented with VAE-based AIGC simulation and degradation-aware passive tamper extraction; robust copyright retrieval is distinct from localization.
image_counts: Localization:1,000 COCO test samples; watermark/fidelity comparison:1,000 UltraEdit512×512 images with paired prompts (§4.3). Tamper extractor20,000 constructed pairs are training data.
metrics: Localization F1/AUC; copyright bit recovery; PSNR/SSIM.
fpr: No fixed numerical image-presence FPR in inspected evaluation. Localization AUC and copyright bit accuracy are different metrics.
quality_practice: Table3 native30/64/100-bit methods with/without extra localization watermark; reports paired quality and recovery, no equal-quality tuning or per-source caliper.
conditional_numbers: Table3 OmniGuard100-bit copyright-only PSNR42.33 SSIM.992 and InstructPix2Pix bit.981; dual watermark PSNR41.78 SSIM.989 bit.979. SD Inpaint* (regenerating outside original content) and strictly local SD Inpaint are explicitly distinct columns.
limitations: Table header labels bit accuracy (%) but entries are fractions such as.981; preserve raw scale and explain as98.1% only when converting. Local edits that retain unedited pixels do not measure full-image independent-encoder regeneration.
reporting_inference: Separate native single-/dual-task arms and attack definitions; captions must name whether unedited pixels were restored.

mechanism: Wavelet decomposition plus spectral projection into high-frequency hidden convolution features; strength-controlled embedding and a learned extractor.
image_counts: 25K COCO images are training data. Main robustness uses DiffusionDB/COCO/DALL·E3 with inherited WAVES setup but per-dataset evaluated n not explicit in inspected main section. Separate social-media/Photoshop check uses200 COCO images. Quality subsets' n is NR.
fpr: WAVES setup is cited, but no explicit numerical image-FPR threshold or negative count stated in inspected§4.2/Table3; do not silently import0.1% as verified implementation.
quality_practice: Resolution256/512/1024 and payload sweeps; native-quality comparisons and attack-quality summary metrics. No exact cross-method paired caliper matching.
conditional_numbers: Table2 clean128-bit SpecGuard PSNR42.89, SSIM.99, FID17.0, BRA.99. Table1 separate30-bit COCO512 quality PSNR44.680/SSIM.9927; the two tables' payloads are not interchangeable.
limitations: Missing exact n and FPR details limit reproduction; bibliographic eligibility does not make every evaluation setting complete. Some comparisons change payload/resolution. Do not infer a common detection test from BRA alone.
reporting_inference: Preserve NR fields rather than backfill convenient inherited settings; include complete denominators and operating points in our own report.

mechanism: Dictionary of initial Gaussian noises; Fourier group identifiers narrow candidate search, then noise similarity validates a match. WINDfull searches all candidates if group search fails; inversion/rotation/crop search is part of detection.
image_counts: Main robustness/quality evaluation-image n remains NR after searching the full available final PDF and reading AppendixD.1–D.9/G/H. N=100,000 in main variants and runtime is dictionary noise/key count; D.1 N=10,000 noises and D.2 N=100 initial noises are likewise not stated as evaluation-image denominators. No count is inferred from decimal accuracy increments.
metrics: Correct watermark/key detection accuracy, cosine similarity, FID; appendix AUC and TPR@1% FPR; PSNR/SSIM for inpainted natural images.
fpr: AppendixD.6/Table11 reports AUC.971 and TP@1%1.000; main key-identification table has a different endpoint. Negative sample count and selected raw similarity cutoff are not explicit in inspected sections.
quality_practice: Same SDv2 and50 generation/inversion steps; FID for generated images, PSNR/SSIM for natural-image inpainting; no exact paired matched-quality comparison.
baselines: Tree-Ring,RingID main;DwtDctSvd,RivaGAN also in FID table;additional methods in appendices.
conditional_numbers: Table1 WINDfull with2048 groups/100000 keys: average accuracy.969, crop&scale.930; WINDfast corresponding crop&scale.060. Table9 natural-image inpainting PSNR26.806/SSIM.768, distinct from generation FID24.33.
limitations: Dictionary size is side information and not payload-bit count or evaluation n. Full versus fast search and generated versus inpainted modes differ materially. Main-image n remains NR rather than guessed from decimal steps. Unresolved internal inconsistency: final Table11 reports AUC .971 and TP@1% 1.000. If both summarize the same standard monotone ROC, TPR=1 at FPR=.01 implies AUC>=.99. Neither rounding nor column extraction resolves this gap; no distinct aggregation explanation was found in inspected AppendixD.6. Preserve both as reported, not coherent calibration evidence. The parent agent rendered and visually inspected final-PDF page 23 on 2026-10-20; cache wind-render/page-023.png confirms the headers and ordering. This is attributed visual verification, not a claim that the T7 author performed that rendering.
reporting_inference: List detector access/search cost and native mode; do not equate different identification and detection operating points or infer independent samples from key count.

evaluation_locator: Final main §4, Tables1–2; separate official supplement §§9–13, Tables3–7 (five pages)
mechanism: Semantic embedding feeds locality-sensitive hashing to derive Gaussian-noise patches; detection compares semantically reconstructed patches with inverted noise, optionally adding a local spatial consistency test.
image_counts: Main removal/CatAttack evaluation-image n remains NR after reading main evaluation and the full available five-page official supplement. Supplement §11 explicitly reports 100 images for latent-forgery attacks only. Supplement §9.4 has 10,000 caption pairs for embedding fine-tuning (training), not test images. n/k=1024 denotes noise patches and b=7 denotes hash bits per patch, not image n.
metrics: ROC-AUC for semantic forgery/CatAttack, removal detection accuracy, steganalysis AUC, and CLIP score before/after watermarking. Different tasks have different denominators.
fpr: Main Tables1–2 report ROC-AUC, not a numerical low-FPR TPR operating point. Supplement §13.3 reports regeneration accuracy, without a numeric FPR/negative denominator. The 100-image latent-forgery experiment does not calibrate rare-image FPR.
quality_practice: Same SDv2/50-step generation+inversion for methods; distribution-free semantic-noise design and attack comparison. No per-source PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS matching in inspected main evaluation.
baselines: Main: WIND, Tree-Ring, Gaussian Shading. Supplement Table6 regeneration: HiDDeN, Stable Signature, TrustMark, WOUAF.
conditional_numbers: Main CatAttack (object dimension30–60% of image): AUC .551 basicSEAL, .982 with spatial test; private-model forgery AUC .708 versus0 for listed baselines. Supplement §11 latent-forgery: complete robustness on100images (author report). Supplement §13.3 Table6 regeneration detection accuracy: SEAL98%, HiDDeN47%, StableSig41%, TrustMark5%, WOUAF51%; image n and FPR are not stated there. Do not combine these tasks into one TPR claim.
limitations: Uses a semantic model and diffusion inversion; semantic binding differs from F5 content-match read endpoint. All five official supplement pages were text-inspected on2026-10-20, including explicit100-image latent-forgery experiment, but main removal/CatAttack n remainsNR. Extraction emitted wrong-pointing-object warnings; relevant prose/tables are coherent, without inferring unavailable figure details. AUC and robustness claims do not supply low-FPR calibration.
reporting_inference: Report content-binding misuse and presence removal separately, and state detector semantic side information; do not treat patch count as statistical sample size.

mechanism: Find non-mutable patches through repeated paraphrases and saliency/stability, then embed Fourier patterns in selected patches/channels with strength depending on region consistency.
image_counts: 500 randomly sampled COCO images using supplied COCO captions; region selection uses SD2.1-base and visual paraphrasing usesSDXL. Five paraphrases for non-mutable patch consistency are part of method selection, not5 independent evaluation cohorts.
metrics: Watermark Detection Probability(WDP), PSNR/SSIM/FID in main table; CLIP/MOS semantic preservation referred to appendix, not independently verified here.
fpr: No numerical image-FPR operating point or negative-image denominator in inspected main§4/Table1. WDP is not automatically TPR at matchedFPR.
quality_practice: Reports different saliency methods/top30/40/50 choices, native quality and paraphrase strengths. Native PSNR differs substantially across baselines; no per-source matched-distortion comparison.
baselines: DwtDctSVD,Stable Signature,WAM,ZoDiac,Tree-Ring,Gaussian Shading and proposed saliency variants.
conditional_numbers: Table1 WAM PSNR46.05/SSIM1.000 and WDP.63/.56 at paraphrase strengths.1/.2; ZoDiac PSNR28.47/SSIM.920 WDP.81/.70; MSI-Net top50 PSNR30.71/SSIM.94 WDP.87/.83. Unequal quality and unspecified imageFPR prevent a fair direct superiority conclusion.
limitations: Official CVF title spellsPECCVAI; paper body spellsPECCAVI. Final venue is verifiedCVPR2026, not inferred from the2025 preprint. Appendix MOS was not read and is not borrowed as a human verdict. Architectural separation alone is not a universal robustness proof.
reporting_inference: Recent independently trained encoder transfer remains a live evaluation theme; insist on quality and image-FPR qualifiers before interpreting a leaderboard, while keeping the present preregistered grid frozen.

mechanism: Optimize an inverted initial latent containing a Fourier watermark through frozen Stable Diffusion, then adaptively blend with original image for SSIM. Detection inverts the suspect and applies a noncentral-chi-square distance test.
image_counts: 500 images each from MS-COCO,DiffusionDB,WikiArt (1,500 distinct source images across domains), evaluated across attacks/settings; primary SD2.1-base50 steps, maximum100 optimization iterations.
metrics: Watermark Detection Rate(WDR=TPR), empirical FPR, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; WDR-versus-native-SSIM trade-offs.
fpr: Table3 COCO: p_star.90/.95/.99 yields measuredFPR.062/.030/.004 and Zhao23WDR.988/.974/.938. Baselines use nominal p<.01 with24/32 or61/96 matching bits. These empiricalFPRs are not equal merely because p-value tests were used.
quality_practice: Adaptive image enhancement and SSIM threshold sweep. Figure3 s_star.8–.98 in.03 increments compares robustness versus native watermark quality; no three-metric per-source caliper match.
conditional_numbers: At p_star.99 Table3 cleanWDR.992, Zhao23.938, All-without-rotation.166, FPR.004. At.90 Zhao23.988 comes withFPR.062; quoting.988 without that false-positive condition is misleading.
limitations: Official venue isNeurIPS2024, neitherECCV norACMMM. Default writer SD2.1 model differs from an independent-encoder regeneration claim. Native-quality enhancement can reduce robustness and cannot be treated as free equalization.
reporting_inference: Preserve native-quality sensitivity as descriptive and show measuredFPR next to every WDR; nominal significance levels across different tests do not guarantee fair actual operating points.
